en: The past that was never actual, a ‘before’ with no date, the pure form of the previous: such are the structural characteristics of the time pertaining to possibility. But such a morphological description is only one first step. The past-form is not, indeed, a mental abstraction (possible to grasp by identifying what the countless particular pasts have in common), nor a mere psychological device. Nothing is less ‘formalistic’ than this form: it does not limit itself to making its mark on many and varied representations, but also exhibits its own particular

. The past-in-general, beyond being a ‘how?’, is also and above all a ‘what?’: it refers to an aspect of existence, and is incarnated in an unavoidable concrete process. Our next task, then, consists in understanding
the past-in-general
, or – the same thing – in naming the potential nestled within it.
zh: 从未成为现实的过去、没有日期的“之前”、在先性的纯粹形式：这些就是可能性之时间的结构特征。然而，这种形态学描述只是第一步。过去形式并不是一种心智抽象——不是从无数具体过去中找出共同点便能把握的东西——也不仅是一种心理装置。没有什么比这种形式更不“形式主义”了：它不只在形形色色的表象上留下印记，还呈现出自身独特的存在方式。一般过去不仅是一个“如何”，更首先是一个“什么”：它指向存在的一个面向，并体现为一个不可避免的具体过程。因此，我们的下一个任务，是理解一般过去究竟是什么；这也就等于说，要为栖居于其中的潜能命名。

en: The past-in-general is, in the first place,

. Meaning: the phonetic, lexical and grammatical system, which exists in the sense of an inexhaustible potential, a potential that is perennial because it is never exhausted or attenuated by the ensemble of its realisations. But the term ‘language’ here has a more extensive – or less rigorous – meaning than Saussure gives it: it also indicates the general disposition towards articulated discourse, the very fact that
speak. Here we are referring to the language
as such, not only the system of signs (
in the strict sense, that is) that allows and mediates its exercise.
zh: 一般过去首先就是语言。这里所谓语言，是指语音、词汇和语法系统；它以一种不可穷尽的潜能而存在，这种潜能之所以恒久不衰，是因为它从不会被其全部现实运用耗尽或削弱。不过，此处“语言”一词的含义比索绪尔赋予它的含义更宽泛——或者说不那么严格：它还指向形成有分节的话语的一般禀赋，也就是我们能够言说这一事实本身。这里所说的是语言官能（language faculty）本身，而不只是使这种官能得以运用并居间调节其运用的符号系统，即严格意义上的语言系统（langue）。

en: According to psychiatrists, people subject to déjà vu are, without exception, inclined to find familiar words strange. Their vocabulary is immobilised, stopping the

phrase in its tracks: derailed from its habitual use, it comes into sharp relief, and produces a sort of echo. We are suddenly struck by certain among its material characteristics (the excess of vowels in ‘queue’, for example), or by the obviousness of its etymology, or by a previously unnoticed homonymy. The familiar word is split in two: we use it to say something, but, at the same time, we put it in inverted commas, as if it were a quotation. It is
but also

; perceived in its actuality, and together with this remembered as something virtual. On the one hand, the mention of the term – simultaneous to its use – situates what is being said in the past. On the other hand, its mention re-evokes the fact that it belongs to the infinite potential of language, restoring the

to the terms of the speakable, and referring the act of speaking back to the faculty that made it possible. On the one hand and the other: but is it really the case that two distinct aspects are at play, here? Or are we talking about one and the same thing? On closer inspection, the mention of the familiar word pushes it back into the

precisely in so far as it reassimilates it to language. And language is, in itself, the purely previous, an indeterminate other-then. The language faculty is the never-present ‘back then’ to which what I now utter can always look back.
zh: 精神病学家指出，容易产生既视感的人无一例外地倾向于把熟悉的词语看成陌生之物。他们的词汇仿佛突然凝固，使句子半途停住：词语脱离了惯常用法，以鲜明轮廓凸显出来，并产生某种回声。我们会突然注意到它的某些物质特征（例如英语 queue 一词中元音字母过多），或它显而易见的词源，或某种此前未曾察觉的同形同音异义现象。熟悉的词一分为二：我们使用它来说某件事，同时又把它放进引号，仿佛它是一段引文。它既被使用，也被提及（use/mention）；既以现实态被知觉，同时又作为潜在之物被记起。一方面，对词项的提及——与使用同时发生——把所说之物安置到过去。另一方面，这种提及重新唤起了词项属于语言之无限潜能这一事实：它把已经说出的东西重新置于可说之物的范围，并把言说的实现追溯到使它成为可能的官能。所谓一方面与另一方面，真的涉及两个不同面向吗？抑或我们谈论的其实是同一件事？细看便会发现：对熟悉词语的提及之所以把它推回不定的过去，恰恰是因为这种提及把它重新归入语言。而语言本身就是纯粹在先之物，就是一个不确定的另一个那时。语言官能就是那个从未成为现在的“那时”，我此刻说出的东西总能回望它。

en: Language is the past-in-general of acts of speaking, the undateable ‘before’ of every specific, unrepeatable utterance. But what goes for linguistic competence also goes – and to the same extent – for whatever other faculty. The potential of the intellect, the simple
towards thought, is the
within which all single intellectual faculties are inscribed. And further: a particular pleasure that I am currently enjoying
nonetheless also exhibits a virtual character, since the memory (of the present) inserts it into the ‘already back then’ constituted by the

to enjoy pleasure. However, considering the complexity of our inclinations, it is not difficult to discern a certain asymmetry here. The memory (of the present, which connects the word spoken or the pleasure enjoyed back to their respective conditions of possibility) in turn has its own condition of possibility (its own
) in the mnestic

. This latter thus plays a pre-eminent role. Memory is the foundation, or the framework, of the past-in-general that we then in each case identify with various different faculties (language, intellect, etc.). To put it in rather awkward, albeit appropriate jargon: mnestic potential is the One of the Many, the genus of the species. The various faculties (being able to speak, being able to enjoy, etc.)
the ‘then already’ – they exhibit a temporal mode of being, because they are part of the memory-One.
zh: 语言是言说实现的一般过去，是每一个具体而不可重复的话语之前那个无法标定日期的“之前”。适用于语言能力的这一点，也同样、同等程度地适用于任何其他官能。智力的潜能，即单纯的思维禀赋，是所有具体智力活动被铭写其中的不定过去。再进一步说：我此刻正在享受的某种特定快感同样显现出潜在性质，因为（对当下的）记忆把它嵌入那个由享受快感的禀赋所构成的“早在那时”。不过，只要考虑到我们各种倾向的复杂性，就不难看出这里存在某种不对称。（对当下的）记忆把说出的词或享受的快感追溯到各自的可能性条件；而这种记忆自身又在记忆官能中拥有它自己的可能性条件，也就是它自己的不定过去。因此，记忆官能具有首要地位。记忆是一般过去的基础或框架；随后，我们才在每一种具体情形中把一般过去分别认作不同的官能（语言、智力，等等）。用一种略显笨拙却颇为恰当的术语来说：记忆潜能是统摄‘多’的‘一’（the One of the Many），是诸种的属。各种官能（能够言说、能够享受，等等）之所以都是“那时已经”、之所以显现出一种时间性的存在方式，是因为它们都属于记忆这一“一”。

en: To avoid ambiguity, it is worth specifying once more that the past-in-general is not a determination of time. The experience of any given faculty does not chronologically precede the experience of the performances that realise it; for instance, we do not notice language if not in relation to some concrete utterance (it strikes us as a
or other-then only at the precise instant in which something is uttered). We could say that the past-in-general is a ‘before’

its ‘then’. But we should add: the very fact that these simultaneous elements give themselves to being seen as ‘before’ and ‘after’ is the unequivocal sign of the radical difference (‘a difference of nature, not degree’) between them. Precisely because it exists as a past-in-general (one that has never
been present), the faculty is not comparable, still less reducible, to the concomitant performance.
zh: 为了避免歧义，值得再次明确：一般过去并不是对时间的某个具体规定。对某种官能的经验并不在年代上先于对实现该官能的活动的经验；例如，我们只有在语言同某个具体话语发生关系时才会注意到语言（唯有在某物被说出的那个准确瞬间，它才会像一个“自古以来”或另一个那时那样击中我们）。可以说，一般过去是一个与其对应的‘随后’同时存在的‘之前’。但还应补充：这些同时存在的要素之所以把自身呈现为“之前”与“之后”，正是它们之间存在根本差别——“性质而非程度上的差别”——的明确标志。官能恰恰因为作为一种从未成为现在的一般过去而存在，才无法与同时发生的实际表现相比较，更无法被还原为后者。
